calculation_handling.description: If a lawfully existing building is longer than the permitted maximum building length, its lawful length becomes its maximum building length.
calculation_handling.gaps: The clause sets the limit to the as-built value of a lawfully existing building but names no date, so it cannot be written with existing(variable; date) without inventing one; keyed UNUSUAL (conservative) rather than as a LIMIT.

units.disclosure: An existing building that is lawfully longer than today's limit may keep its length; we cannot check existing building lengths.

calculation_handling.description: An addition or extension to a lawfully existing building relying on 10.5.40.21(1) must comply with all other regulations or be authorized by a minor variance.
calculation_handling.gaps: Zones left empty: the unit text names no zone (10.5 = Residential Zone category).

units.disclosure: Additions to a building that relies on its existing length must meet all other rules or get a minor variance.

10.5.40.21(1).explanation: If an existing building was lawfully built longer than the current maximum building length, its existing length is treated as its allowed maximum.

10.5.40.21(2).explanation: Any addition to such a building must meet all other zoning rules or be approved through a minor variance.
